normalized.governing_thought: Yes, raise prices in 2027, but not 12% on every plan: price mid-market and enterprise now, and hold SMB until the evidence is in
executive_summary: Churn is a cohort problem, not a market-wide price problem

SMB monthly churn rose 2.0% → 3.1%; ~90% of the rise comes from the 2,100 customers who joined on the 2025 50%-off promotion. Other SMB customers churn at 2.1% (2.0% a year ago) and only 18% of them cite price (19% in 2025). Mid-market 0.6% → 0.8%; enterprise flat at 0.2%.
The headroom is in mid-market and enterprise

76% of ARR, net revenue retention (NRR) of 112% and 118%; customers stay for integrations and the audit trail; a +10% price test showed no significant conversion loss. SMB is where Inkwell's $9 plan is winning: win rate 51% → 38%.
Only $7.6M can be repriced in 2027 (15% of mid-market and 60% of enterprise ARR do not renew; enterprise caps at 7%). After the likely churn response it is $4.5–6.3M.

Mid-market +10% at renewal; enterprise at contract terms (7% where capped, 10% otherwise): +$4.3M. SMB list price held through June while a controlled +8% test runs; go or no-go for the second half (+$0.4M). Activation programme for the promotion cohort (+$0.3M). ≈ $98.9M exit ARR, exactly the +15% target, before any new-customer ARR; NRR ≈ 115%.

≈ $1.6M less 2027 ARR than the CFO plan's base case on paper. In exchange: no wider price gap against Inkwell where Palisade is losing deals, and a measured answer on SMB price sensitivity before 5,900 customers are committed to it.
Decisions needed in December: approve mid-market and enterprise renewal pricing · hold SMB and approve the test and June gate · fund the activation programme · restate the board churn metric

slides.title: The CFO's $10.3M assumes all ARR reprices in 2027; renewal timing and contract caps cut it to $7.6M, and churn to $4.5–6.3M

claims.claim: Bridge of ARR gained from +12% on every plan in 2027, $M
Renewal timing. Price changes apply at renewal; 85% of mid-market and 40% of enterprise ARR renew in 2027.
Contract caps. 60% of enterprise ARR cannot rise more than 7% a year.
SMB churn. In 2023, +8% raised SMB churn by 0.5 pts for six months and 0.1 pts after; scaled to 12% that loses ~5% of SMB ARR.
Not counted: any loss of new SMB deals to Inkwell from a higher list price.
SMB is the weak link: of its $2.5M gross gain, $1.3M (base) to $2.5M (downside) goes back out as churn.

Main risk: SMB deals and promotion-cohort churn; 2027 churn signal becomes hard to read

claims.claim: B · Hold prices, fix onboarding — NOT RECOMMENDED
evidence: Main risk: Misses the target unless new-customer ARR is ≥ $4.7M; leaves mid-market and enterprise headroom unused

claims.claim: C · Segmented increase — RECOMMENDED
evidence: Mid-market +10%, enterprise at terms from January; SMB +8% from July only if the test passes
SMB exposure: None until July; +8% for the core base only if the test passes; promotion cohort deferred to 2028
Main risk: ≈ $1.6M below A in the base case; downside needs ≥ $1.1M of new-customer ARR

claims.claim: All options include promotion-cohort activation (+$0.3M). Base = $86.0M × each segment's trailing NRR = $94.0M. Downside = stronger churn response, no activation gain, SMB test fails.

slides.title: The recommended plan reaches the +15% target ($98.9M) before any new-customer ARR, but with no margin to spare

claims.claim: Exit-2027 ARR bridge, base case, $M
Downside: $97.8M. Mid-market reacts at renewal, activation gains nothing, the SMB test fails. Closing the gap needs ≥ $1.1M of new-customer ARR.

Timing: each month of renewals missed because notice periods have passed costs ≈ $0.36M.

claims.claim: An answer to the biggest open question. How price-sensitive the core SMB base is now that Inkwell exists, measured before committing all 5,900 customers.
No wider gap at the point of sale. SMB win rate against Inkwell is already down 13 points; neither A nor C counts the effect on new deals.
A clean read on onboarding. With SMB prices unchanged, 2027 churn shows whether activation works.

Where the CFO is right: the churn rise is mostly an onboarding and cohort problem. That is why mid-market and enterprise go ahead in January.
In the downside case the January SMB rise nets ≈ $0: $2.5M of extra churn cancels $2.5M of price. Deferring it costs at most ≈ $0.85M.

slides.title: How: mid-market and enterprise renewals start in January, SMB is tested in the first half, and leadership decides in June

claims.claim: Mid-market and enterprise pricing: notices in December, then mid-market +10% and enterprise at terms applied at each renewal (Owner: CFO + Sales)
SMB price test: design, then +8% test on new sign-ups and a 10% sample of renewals; if go: +8% list; core base at renewal (Owner: Growth / Product)
Promotion-cohort activation: activation programme; targets by end-June; continue if targets met (Owner: Customer Success)
Metrics and governance: define churn; monthly guardrail review (Owner: CFO)

slides.title: Guardrails tell us early whether to pause, extend or stop each move

claims.claim: Mid-market +10% guardrails
evidence: Monthly logo churn of renewing mid-market accounts; today 0.8%; > 1.0% for two months running → Pause rises on remaining renewals; offer a multi-year price lock instead
≤ 0.8% through June → Renew the second half at +12% (+$0.35M)

claims.claim: Enterprise at terms guardrail
evidence: Renewal outcome of each top account; today 0.2% churn; NRR 118%; Any renewal flagged at risk → Trade the increase for a longer term; never breach the 7% cap

claims.claim: SMB +8% test (June gate)
evidence: Conversion at +8% vs control; churn of renewal sample vs control; price share of core churners; today 2.1% core churn; 18% cite price
Go only if conversion is not significantly lower, sample churn ≤ control + 0.3 pts and price share ≤ 20%
Go: +8% from July for the core base. No-go: hold through 2027 and build a packaging answer to Inkwell for 2028

claims.claim: Promotion-cohort activation guardrail
evidence: Share sending ≥5 documents a month; cohort monthly churn; today 41%; ≈4.9%
If missed, stop extra spend; plan on ≈45% of the cohort's ARR ($2.0M) leaving within 12 months

claims.claim: Competitive position guardrail
evidence: SMB win rate where Inkwell is considered; today 38%; < 35% → Bring the 2028 SMB packaging review forward

claims.claim: Thresholds are our proposal for leadership to confirm; the pack gives today's values only. Review monthly at the pricing steering meeting.

slides.title: Three open questions could change the plan; each has a built-in test

claims.claim: How price-sensitive is the core SMB base now that Inkwell exists?
evidence: If the test is clean: +8% from July, and SMB returns to the 2028 plan. If not: hold, and work on packaging rather than list price.

claims.claim: Can the promotion cohort be activated, or will it mostly churn anyway?
evidence: Activation explains under a third of its excess churn.
If targets are missed by June, stop extra spend. Its losses are already in the baseline NRR; a reverting cohort is upside.

claims.claim: Does the 2024 mid-market test (new sign-ups) predict renewals?
evidence: Existing customers may react differently from new buyers.
The guardrail on renewing accounts gives a first read in Q1. Pause if churn exceeds 1.0%; extend to 12% if it holds.

claims.claim: Gaps in the evidence to close before the board meeting
evidence: New-customer ARR plan for 2027: Not in the pack. The downside case needs ≥ $1.1M of it to reach +15%.
Renewal notice periods: Each month of renewals missed costs ≈ $0.36M of the $4.3M.
Board churn metric: “1.4% → 2.3%” cannot be rebuilt from segment data (appendix).

slides.title: Five decisions for the leadership team in December

claims.claim: APPROVE: Mid-market +10% at renewal and enterprise increases at contract terms (7% where capped, 10% target otherwise), effective with January 2027 renewals. (CFO, Sales)
REJECT: The +12% rise on every plan. Hold SMB list prices through June 2027; exclude the promotion cohort from any 2027 increase. (CEO)
APPROVE: The SMB +8% test (February–May) and the June go or no-go gate with the criteria on page 13. (Growth / Product)
FUND: The promotion-cohort activation programme, with targets on activation (≥55%) and cohort churn (≤4.0%), not “halve SMB churn”. (Customer Success)
FIX: The board churn metric: report logo and revenue churn by segment, and confirm the 2027 new-customer ARR plan. (CFO, Sales)
Result: ≈ $98.9M exit ARR (+15%) before new customers, NRR ≈ 115%, and the SMB price decision taken in June on evidence rather than on the 2023 analogue.

normalized.recommendation: Segmented increase (option C): mid-market +10% at renewal and enterprise at contract terms (7% where capped, 10% otherwise) from January 2027; reject the +12% rise on every plan; hold SMB list prices through June 2027 while a controlled +8% test runs, with a June go or no-go gate (SMB +8% from July only if the test passes); exclude the promotion cohort from any 2027 increase; fund the promotion-cohort activation programme with targets on activation (≥55%) and cohort churn (≤4.0%); fix the board churn metric (report logo and revenue churn by segment) and confirm the 2027 new-customer ARR plan.

normalized.extraction_notes: The deck came as plain text with no images. On slides 3, 4, 5, 7, 9, 10, 11 and 12, chart axis ticks and data labels were pulled out as separate lines. I matched values to their categories by their order and by the category labels and footnotes. On slide 4, I took the +0.1% and +1.0% bridge steps to mean the core drift and the cohort mix effect. On slide 10, I worked out the bar order (1.25, +0.77, −0.40, 1.62) from the labels. On slide 12, I placed the Gantt timing (Dec–Dec months) from its labels only; the exact bar spans were not available. On slide 15, the APPROVE/REJECT/FUND/FIX labels appear out of order in the extraction, so I matched them to decisions by their order and meaning.
